name: Chest of Containment Coffers
summary: Mages in the Undercity keep the Chest of Containment Coffers close at hand. Its enchanted vessels can secure unstable magical phenomena.

sections.title: Vessels for the Unseen
sections.body: Invisible arcane creatures can emerge from experiments or sudden rifts between planes. Ordinary cages cannot hold beings made of magic. The Chest of Containment Coffers holds enchanted vessels that bind subdued creatures alive. Senior instructors keep the chest nearby, including Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity and Jennea Cannon in Stormwind. They give initiates the coffers for surveying anomalies before those forces can unsettle their surroundings.

sections.title: Arcane Containment Protocols
sections.body: Invisible disturbances appeared in Algernon's shop in the Apothecarium, and Forsaken instructors sent mages with coffers to contain them. A mage first reveals a rift entity with a special scroll, then weakens it with spells and traps it in a coffer from the chest. Forsaken researchers can safely dissect and study the captured creatures, determining whether the disturbances were random tears in the Ley or deliberate arcane assaults.

faq.q: What is inside the Chest of Containment Coffers?
faq.answer: The chest holds empty, enchanted coffers. Mages use them to secure and trap subdued magical creatures, such as rift spawns, during dangerous field investigations.

faq.q: Where can this chest be found?
faq.answer: In the Undercity, the chest sits behind Mage Trainer Anastasia Hartwell in the Magic Quarter. A matching chest is behind Jennea Cannon in the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind City.

faq.q: Why do mages need these coffers instead of normal cages?
faq.answer: Rift spawns are made of intangible arcane energy, which ordinary materials cannot hold. Enchanted coffers can trap and stabilize these anomalies.

faq.q: What happens to the coffers once they are filled?
aliases: what happens to captured rift spawns
faq.answer: Senior instructors receive filled coffers for study. Researchers analyze the captured creatures to determine whether a disturbance came from an accidental natural rift or an intentional attack by outside forces.

angles.text: As a mage, you can use these field tools to manage volatile arcane manifestations and preserve living specimens for study.
As Forsaken, you can use these coffers to secure magical anomalies near the Apothecarium, keeping unvetted arcane forces from corrupting your work.
